questions: How long does meth stay in the blood?
answers.short: After the blood level peaks, it takes about 10 to 12 hours to fall by half.
answers.but: It differs from person to person, and it is not the same as how long the effects last.

questions: How fast do the effects of a snorted dose peak?
answers.short: Snorted, its effects on the heart and on mood peak within about 15 minutes.
answers.but: The amount in the blood keeps rising for hours. The timing of the effects comes from one lab.

questions: What does meth do in the brain?
answers.short: It makes nerve cells let out three brain chemicals: dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin.
answers.but: How it does this is not fully known. So far we have only read a review about it.

questions: How much reaches the blood when it is snorted or smoked?
answers.short: Most of a snorted dose reaches the blood. For smoking, the figures vary a lot.
answers.but: The snorting figure comes from one study of 8 men. For smoking, studies measure it in different ways.

questions: Do the two mirror-image forms of meth act differently?
answers.short: Yes: in one study, the 'l' form felt weaker and its effects ended sooner.
answers.but: One small lab study of injected doses in 12 men.

questions: What does one dose of meth do to the body and mood?
answers.short: One snorted dose raises heart rate and blood pressure and makes people feel high.
answers.but: These were single lab doses in people used to meth, not binges. One lab only.

questions: Does one dose of meth make thinking worse at the time?
answers.short: In lab tests, single doses did not measurably worsen attention or memory.
answers.but: The studies were small, so small or moderate harm can't be ruled out. Binges were not tested.

questions: Do meth's effects fade while it is still in the blood?
answers.short: The good feelings fade within one dose and within three days; hunger stays gone.
answers.but: All of this used small oral doses in six to nine people in a laboratory.

questions: Does meth reduce appetite?
answers.short: One dose cut how much people ate that day by about two fifths.
answers.but: One small study of eight people living in a lab.

questions: What does a meth overdose look like?
answers.short: A meth overdose can look like a body in overdrive. The heart races, breathing speeds up, and people get very restless and upset. Some lose touch with reality.
answers.but: That's second-hand, from two reviews of hospital studies, and how often each sign shows up varies a lot.

questions: How many people who use stimulants like meth get hooked?
answers.short: It depends how you count. An old US survey found 11 in 100 had ever been dependent; a broader Australian count estimated about 50 in 100 within 14 years of starting.
answers.but: Neither survey has a number for meth alone, and the two measured different things, so they can't be compared directly.

questions: Do people who use meth always pick the drug over cash?
answers.short: In lab choice tests, people often chose small amounts of cash over a stimulant dose.
answers.but: Only 13 men, in one lab. Different men got different cash amounts, so it can't show what more cash does.

questions: What is meth withdrawal like, and how long does it last?
answers.short: After stopping, most symptoms people reported eased within one to two weeks. Low mood and craving lasted longer.
answers.but: It was one small study on a hospital ward. The people in it were not seeking treatment.

questions: Does meth damage dopamine nerve cells?
answers.short: Nobody has shown either way whether meth, as people use it, damages dopamine nerve cells.
answers.but: Scans show changes, but those can happen without nerve cells dying. Experts disagree.

questions: Is the dopamine system different in people who used meth heavily?
answers.short: People who used meth heavily have less of one dopamine protein on scans than people who don't, on average.
answers.but: Scans cannot tell if this is damage, the brain making less of the protein, or a difference from before use.

questions: Do dopamine changes in people who used meth recover after stopping?
answers.short: In five people, that protein rose after a year without meth.
answers.but: Only five people, with nobody who doesn't use scanned twice. Four other small studies found no link with time off meth.

questions: What do scans of the brain's dopamine-storage protein show after meth?
answers.short: A few days after use, another dopamine marker looks higher. After about 10 days off meth, it is not clearly different.
answers.but: Researchers think this shows low stored dopamine, which the study could not test. One lab only, and the studies are small.

questions: Do people who used meth have less grey matter?
answers.short: Some brain areas looked smaller soon after stopping. Other studies found some larger.
answers.but: Smoking, schooling and low mood also differ, and some differences may not last.

questions: Is brain activity different in people who have stopped using meth?
answers.short: The results are mixed: the differences found were small, uncertain or not repeated.
answers.but: The groups also differed in smoking and in other ways. That could explain the results.

questions: Does brain activity change after a year without meth?
answers.short: In five people, one deep brain area got more active after a year off meth, compared with the rest of the brain.
answers.but: Only five people, with no group to compare. The paper's numbers also have errors.

questions: Could brain differences seen in stimulant dependence be there before drug use?
answers.short: Brothers and sisters who never had drug or alcohol problems shared some brain differences with their sibling dependent on stimulants.
answers.but: One study, and 94 in 100 of the dependent people were dependent on cocaine.

questions: Is meth linked to Parkinson's disease?
answers.short: Parkinson's was diagnosed more often in people with a meth or amphetamine diagnosis and no other drug or alcohol diagnosis.
answers.but: It stays rare: about 3 in 1,000 over about 7 years. Some diagnoses are probably other conditions, and medicine side effects were not ruled out.

questions: Do people dependent on meth score lower on memory and thinking tests?
answers.short: On average, people dependent on meth score somewhat lower on memory and thinking tests than healthy volunteers.
answers.but: This does not show that meth caused it. Group averages are mostly still in the normal range.

questions: Are thinking-test scores of people dependent on meth in the normal range?
answers.short: On average, their scores were in the normal range, not the impaired range.
answers.but: Some people did score low. And nobody was tested before they started using.

questions: Does meth cause lasting problems with thinking and memory?
answers.short: It has not been shown that meth causes lasting problems with thinking and memory in people.
answers.but: Nobody was tested before use, and the groups differ in other ways. Experts disagree.

questions: Do memory and thinking get better after stopping meth?
answers.short: We don't know yet. In retests, people who stopped did not clearly improve more than people who don't use.
answers.but: Only two small studies also retested people who don't use, so a moderate gain can't be ruled out. Very few looked beyond a year.

questions: Is meth linked to psychosis?
answers.short: Psychotic symptoms are more common in people who use meth, most of all in those who use it often.
answers.but: No study has settled which comes first.

questions: In people dependent on meth, is frequent use linked to psychotic symptoms?
answers.short: In people dependent on meth, psychotic symptoms were much more common in months of heavy use.
answers.but: One study. It cannot prove that the drug caused the symptoms.

questions: How long does meth-related psychosis last?
answers.short: In a typical study of people with meth psychosis, about 1 in 4 still had symptoms over a month after stopping.
answers.but: Studies ranged from none to almost all, and most were of hospital patients.

questions: How does meth psychosis compare with schizophrenia?
answers.short: Meth psychosis and schizophrenia can look alike.
answers.but: Flatness and withdrawal were milder in meth psychosis. No symptom has been shown to reliably tell them apart.

questions: Is meth linked to depression?
answers.short: People who use meth report low mood somewhat more often than people who don't.
answers.but: Other differences, such as using other drugs or a hard life, may explain part of it: against people who use other drugs, there was no clear difference.

questions: Is meth use linked to suicidal thoughts and attempts?
answers.short: People with a meth use disorder report suicidal thoughts and attempts more often.
answers.but: Most studies were of people in emergency rooms, the justice system or treatment. Drug use in general and earlier problems may explain much of it.

questions: Is meth linked to violence?
answers.short: Two long-term studies linked meth use to more violence. This held after other things were counted.
answers.but: Both studies share authors, and neither could show which came first.

questions: Does naltrexone with bupropion help people stay off meth during treatment?
answers.short: In one big trial, for every 9 people given two medicines, about 1 more had mostly meth-free urine tests.
answers.but: Most people were not helped. What happened after treatment ended was not reported.

questions: Does the antidepressant mirtazapine help people use less meth?
answers.short: In three trials, people on a depression medicine, mirtazapine, used somewhat less meth than on a dummy pill.
answers.but: Most people kept using, and in the largest trial drug tests showed no difference.

questions: Do bupropion or modafinil help people stop using meth?
answers.short: Bupropion and modafinil did not help more people stop than a dummy pill.
answers.but: The trials were small, so a modest benefit or harm cannot be ruled out.

questions: Do any medicines ease meth withdrawal?
answers.short: No medicine on sale has clearly been shown to ease meth withdrawal.
answers.but: The trials were few and small, so a benefit cannot be ruled out either.

questions: Have any medicines been shown to help meth psychosis?
answers.short: Few trials have tested medicines for meth psychosis: eight small, short ones and one longer one.
answers.but: None of the short trials had a dummy-pill group, so they can't show if medicines help more than stopping meth. Some have serious flaws.

questions: How many people who use meth or amphetamine regularly die each year?
answers.short: Among people with regular or problematic use, about 1 in 90 died each year.
answers.but: These were people in treatment, in hospital or justice records, or who inject, not everyone who uses. Not all of it is the drug.

questions: Have meth use and meth deaths risen in the US?
answers.short: In the US, meth use rose from 2015 to 2019, and deaths involving meth kept rising through 2023, the latest year counted.
answers.but: Many of these deaths also involved fentanyl or other opioids. The rise slowed after 2021.

questions: Is a serotonin by-product lower in people who use MDMA?
answers.short: In one study, a serotonin by-product in spinal fluid was lower in people who used MDMA.
answers.but: It was clear only in the women, and that group had used many other drugs too.

questions: Do people who use ecstasy score lower on memory tests?
answers.short: On average, people who use ecstasy score lower on some memory and thinking tests.
answers.but: The studies disagree a lot, and none can show that ecstasy caused it.

questions: Are lower memory scores due to ecstasy, or to other drugs?
answers.short: In people who used ecstasy but hardly any other drug, memory scores were no different.
answers.but: It was one study, and medium-sized differences could not be ruled out.

questions: Does memory change when people start using ecstasy?
answers.short: In one Dutch study, people who started using ecstasy improved less on a word-memory test.
answers.but: They also used more cannabis and cocaine, and were tested again sooner.

questions: Does memory recover after people stop using ecstasy?
answers.short: Nobody knows yet whether scores recover after people stop using ecstasy.
answers.but: The studies compared different people, not the same people over time.

questions: Do brain scans show serotonin changes in people who use ecstasy?
answers.short: Scans show less of a serotonin marker in people who use ecstasy.
answers.but: Nobody in these studies was scanned before they started, and these groups also used more other drugs.

questions: What happened to the famous 2002 study claiming ecstasy damaged monkeys' brains?
answers.short: A 2002 study said ecstasy harmed monkeys' brains. It was withdrawn a year later.
answers.but: Fewer newspapers told readers about the mistake than told the first story.

questions: Does ecstasy damage dopamine nerve cells?
answers.short: It has not been shown that ecstasy harms dopamine nerve cells in people.
answers.but: Very little has been measured in people, so this does not show it is safe.

questions: Does ecstasy harm the brain for good?
answers.short: Experts disagree about whether ecstasy leaves lasting harm to the serotonin system.
answers.but: Almost nobody was scanned before they started, so a difference may have come first.

questions: Is meth use linked to crime?
answers.short: People dependent on meth reported more crime in months when they used it.
answers.but: One study, and it could not show which came first.

questions: Does MDMA-assisted therapy help PTSD more than therapy with a dummy pill?
answers.short: Yes, in two trials. With the same therapy, 61 to 70 in 100 no longer had PTSD after MDMA, against 27 to 39 in 100 after a dummy pill.
answers.but: In the trial that asked, most knew which pill they'd had, so expectations may explain part of the gap.

questions: Could people in the trials tell if they got MDMA?
answers.short: In the trial that asked, most people could tell MDMA from the dummy pill.
answers.but: Only one of the two trials asked, and only at the very end.

questions: What side effects did MDMA cause in the PTSD trials?
answers.short: MDMA often gave brief side effects, like tight muscles, feeling sick and sweating.
answers.but: The trials were too small and short to show rare or later harms.

questions: Did the US regulator approve MDMA therapy for PTSD in 2024?
answers.short: No. The US regulator turned it down in August 2024, after its expert panel voted 9 to 2 that the data didn't show it works.
answers.but: We read the panel's notes, but we only know the decision second-hand.

questions: Why were three earlier MDMA therapy studies withdrawn?
answers.short: In 2024 a journal withdrew three earlier studies from the MDMA therapy research.
answers.but: The journal did not say how much of the data came from that site.

questions: Is MDMA therapy good value for money?
answers.short: Two critics say price and comparison decide if MDMA therapy is good value.
answers.but: The cost studies come from the company or from people with money ties to it.

questions: Do the MDMA therapy trials hold up?
answers.short: It's not settled. Two trials found PTSD eased more with MDMA than with a dummy pill, but can't show how much was the drug itself, or for how long.
answers.but: One sponsor ran both trials, and in the one that asked, most people knew their pill.

questions: Does the benefit of MDMA therapy for PTSD last?
answers.short: Months to years later, people who had MDMA still scored lower on PTSD.
answers.but: Only about 7 in 10 came back for one check, and many had other treatments in between.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help people with alcohol problems?
answers.short: In one small study, 9 of 14 people drank much less after MDMA therapy.
answers.but: There was no group without MDMA. And all had just been through detox.

questions: Does MDMA therapy ease anxiety in people with a serious illness?
answers.short: In one small trial, anxiety fell more with MDMA than with a dummy pill.
answers.but: The difference could be chance: only 18 people took part, and most could tell which pill they had.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help social anxiety in autistic adults?
answers.short: In one small trial, social anxiety eased more with MDMA than with a dummy pill.
answers.but: Only 12 autistic adults took part, and almost all could tell which pill they got.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help couples where one partner has PTSD?
answers.short: After couples therapy with MDMA, PTSD eased and couples were happier.
answers.but: Neither study had a group without MDMA. And this couples therapy helps PTSD even without it.

questions: Does MDMA therapy help depression?
answers.short: In one small study, depression dropped a lot after two MDMA sessions.
answers.but: There was no group without MDMA. And the people who scored depression knew everyone had taken it.

questions: Did MDMA therapy for PTSD change people's drinking or drug use?
answers.short: MDMA therapy for PTSD did not clearly change drinking or drug use.
answers.but: Almost no one had a drinking or drug problem to start with. And people reported their own use.

questions: What side effects did MDMA cause in trials outside PTSD?
answers.short: In small trials, MDMA's side effects were common and brief, and none were serious.
answers.but: These trials were too small to show rare or later harms.

questions: In the early MDMA trials for PTSD, did the benefit last?
answers.short: In two sets of early PTSD trials, average PTSD scores stayed about as low as at the end of MDMA therapy a year or more later.
answers.but: There was no comparison group, many people also had other therapy or medicines, and the same sponsor ran both studies.

questions: Does MDMA therapy for PTSD change sleep?
answers.short: In early PTSD trials, people who had full doses of MDMA said they slept better than people who had a very small dose.
answers.but: The trials were small, no one checked whether people could tell which dose they had, and the results had to be corrected after an ethics breach at one site.

questions: What side effects does MDMA cause in therapy trials?
answers.short: Common ones were a tight jaw, anxiety, less appetite, feeling sick and sweating. They happened during sessions and in the week after. Most were mild to moderate and soon passed.
answers.but: The record is patchy. Most studies only noted problems people raised themselves. Some never reached the papers, and later risks are barely known.

questions: Can MDMA therapy help with anything besides PTSD?
answers.short: Nobody can say yet. Outside PTSD, it's been tried for a few things. They include tinnitus, drinking problems, and anxiety in autistic adults or in people who are very ill.
answers.but: Each had one tiny trial at most, the biggest with 18 people.

questions: How was MDMA used in therapy before it was banned?
answers.short: Before MDMA was banned in 1985, a few dozen US therapists used it in talking therapy.
answers.but: This comes second-hand from one history review, and the reports of the time were not designed well enough to show whether MDMA helped.

questions: What happens when meth and alcohol are taken together?
Meth with alcohol: what changes?
answers.short: With alcohol, meth raises the heart rate more and makes people feel less drunk.
answers.but: One study of nine men, with small oral doses in a laboratory.

questions: Does a second dose work like the first?
answers.short: A second dose raises the drug in your blood, but not the strongest feeling.
answers.but: Three small laboratory studies, 9 to 23 people, and none gave more than two doses.

questions: Does MDMA stop working as well with regular use?
answers.short: Most people who keep using ecstasy say it stops working as well.
answers.but: This comes from questionnaires, retold in one review; no laboratory study has tested it.

questions: What does a second dose do to the heart and body?
answers.short: Taking more adds strain on the heart and blood pressure without stronger good feelings.
answers.but: Small laboratory studies of healthy, screened people sitting in a quiet room.

questions: Opioids with benzodiazepines: how much riskier?
answers.short: People on prescribed opioids and benzos had more overdoses than people on opioids alone.
answers.but: The studies could not separate the benzos from the reasons people were given them.

questions: How many opioid deaths also involve benzodiazepines?
answers.short: About 1 in 5 US opioid overdose deaths in 2017 also involved benzos.
answers.but: Death records miss some drugs, and a share of deaths does not measure risk.

questions: How many opioid deaths also involve alcohol?
answers.short: Alcohol was listed in about 1 in 7 US opioid overdose deaths.
answers.but: Alcohol is often left off death records, and these counts do not measure risk.

questions: On methadone or buprenorphine and also prescribed sedatives?
answers.short: In UK methadone or buprenorphine treatment, benzo prescriptions were linked to more poisoning deaths.
answers.but: The study did not take mental health, alcohol or street drug use into account.

questions: Is the change bigger in people who have used more?
answers.short: People who had taken more ecstasy showed less of the serotonin marker.
answers.but: The amounts come from memory, and people who take more ecstasy take more of everything else.

questions: After stopping ecstasy, do serotonin changes on scans return to normal?
answers.short: We do not know if the marker goes back to normal after people stop.
answers.but: Nobody has been scanned while using and then again years later.

questions: Do brain scans change when people first start using ecstasy?
answers.short: In one study, a few pills did not change the serotonin marker.
answers.but: Most of these people had taken only one or two pills in all.

questions: Opioids with gabapentin or pregabalin: how much riskier?
answers.short: Gabapentin or pregabalin with opioid painkillers was linked to more opioid overdose deaths in Ontario.
answers.but: Both Ontario studies are from one team and do not say why people were given the medicines.

questions: What does MDMA do to body temperature, heart and blood pressure?
answers.short: One dose pushes all three up. In lab tests, 24 in 100 people went over 38 degrees after MDMA, against 9 in 100 after a dummy pill.
answers.but: Healthy volunteers rested in a room at about 23 degrees. Heat, dancing, crowds, other drugs and extra doses weren't tested.

questions: Why do some people overheat on MDMA?
answers.short: Nobody can yet say why some people get hotter than others with MDMA.
answers.but: This is second-hand, from one review of small studies. They couldn't tell heat, dancing and crowds apart.

questions: Can drinking lots of water on MDMA lead to low blood salt?
answers.short: Possibly. Low blood salt (sodium) after MDMA has been reported, mostly in young people; of 17 UK cases, at least 10 had drunk a lot of liquid.
answers.but: These only count people who got ill, so they can't show how often it happens, or whether drinking more changes the risk.

questions: Is low blood salt after MDMA more common in women?
answers.short: Yes, among people who got ill: 52 in 100 women tested had low blood salt, against 22 in 100 men, in one poison-centre study.
answers.but: It counts only people ill enough to be reported and tested, so it can't say who's most at risk among everyone who takes MDMA.

questions: What can MDMA do to the kidneys?
answers.short: Kidney injury after MDMA has been reported in single cases; nobody knows how often.
answers.but: This is second-hand, from reviews of case reports, which cannot show how often it happens.

questions: Is ecstasy really MDMA, and how strong are the pills?
answers.short: Ecstasy pills are often MDMA, but not always, and the amount varies a lot.
answers.but: These tests end around 2002, so they may not describe pills today.

questions: Can people become dependent on ecstasy?
answers.short: Yes, some do. How many depends on who's asked: about 4 in 100 people who'd used it recently in US surveys, but up to 73 in 100 in small groups.
answers.but: Every checklist was made for other drugs, and most studies used volunteers, so the numbers can't be applied to everyone who uses ecstasy.

questions: Can regular heavy MDMA use harm the heart valves?
answers.short: Heart valve changes were more common in people who had taken MDMA, in one small study.
answers.but: Nobody was scanned before taking MDMA, so this cannot show that MDMA caused it.

questions: In MDMA deaths, which medicines were found too?
answers.short: Among 19 Australian deaths with MDMA and a risky mix, antidepressants, opioids and benzos were common.
answers.but: The 19 were picked for risky mixes, so the counts do not show how common any mix is.

questions: What is serotonin syndrome, and how do doctors spot it?
answers.short: Doctors look for muscle jerks, shaking, sweating and restlessness when serotonin may be too high.
answers.but: The checklist was tested in one hospital unit, on overdoses, against that unit's own diagnosis.

questions: What about MAOI antidepressants, like moclobemide?
MDMA with MAOI antidepressants such as moclobemide?
answers.short: Four young people in Finland died with MDMA and moclobemide, an antidepressant, in their blood.
answers.but: Four deaths cannot give a rate, and all four also had other drugs in their blood or urine.

questions: What about other drugs that raise serotonin?
Which drugs add to MDMA's serotonin risk?
answers.short: One 2007 review ranked drugs by serotonin risk with ecstasy: MAOIs highest, SSRIs lower.
answers.but: This is the authors' judgment from reports and how the drugs work, not from counts of people.

questions: Opioid painkillers with MAOI antidepressants?
answers.short: Reports link pethidine and tramadol to bad reactions with MAOI antidepressants; none for morphine.
answers.but: It rests on old case reports in reviews; nobody has counted how often it happens.

questions: What happens when cocaine and alcohol are used together?
Cocaine with alcohol: what happens to the heart?
answers.short: Together they make a new substance, cocaethylene, and hearts beat faster than with cocaine alone.
answers.but: Small hospital studies of 8 and 6 people. None measured heart attacks or rhythm problems.

questions: Can cocaine make someone feel less drunk?
Does cocaine hide how drunk someone is?
answers.short: People given cocaine with alcohol did not feel more drunk, and sometimes slightly less.
answers.but: This is second-hand from one review of small studies, and no one tested driving.

questions: Why can the usual amount be dangerous after a break?
answers.short: Tolerance may drop during a break from opioids, two reviews say. So the usual amount may hit much harder, breathing included.
answers.but: The reviews give no numbers. Not how long a break must be, or how much the risk of a fatal overdose rises.

questions: What happens with SSRI antidepressants?
answers.short: An SSRI muted MDMA's effects in lab tests; with paroxetine, MDMA blood levels rose.
answers.but: Only 28 healthy volunteers were tested, for a few days at most, and no one was given more MDMA.

questions: What about other antidepressants?
answers.short: Other antidepressants did not act alike: some muted MDMA's effects, and bupropion did not.
answers.but: These numbers are second-hand, from a 2022 review of single trials with 16 healthy people each.

questions: What do case reports say about mixing with medicines?
answers.short: In safety reports, ecstasy cases that also named an antidepressant ended in death more often.
answers.but: Voluntary reports cannot show cause, and nobody knows how many people took each mix.

questions: What about other psychiatric medicines?
answers.short: Few other psychiatric medicines were tested with MDMA, and the results differ by medicine.
answers.but: Each was tested once in 14 to 16 healthy people, and the results come second-hand from a 2022 review.

questions: Why do some bodies, or some medicines, make MDMA stronger?
answers.short: MDMA seems to switch off the enzyme that clears it, so body differences matter less.
answers.but: Only 7 people had no working enzyme, and no study gave a second dose of MDMA.

questions: Does taking more MDMA raise blood levels more than you'd expect?
answers.short: Yes, it seems so: a dose 1.67 times larger gave a peak blood level 1.8 times higher, and about twice the total over the day.
answers.but: Only 8 men were compared, in a lab, and the study was not planned to look at this.

questions: Is using ecstasy in pregnancy linked to birth defects?
answers.short: One study counted birth defects after ecstasy in pregnancy, but it cannot show cause.
answers.but: There was no comparison group, and almost half of the enquiries were lost to follow-up.

questions: How do babies exposed to ecstasy in pregnancy do in their first months?
answers.short: At 1 and 4 months, babies of women who used ecstasy mostly scored the same.
answers.but: The mothers also used more cocaine, cannabis, tobacco and alcohol, and only 22 exposed babies were seen.

questions: Cannabis with alcohol: is driving worse than with either alone?
answers.short: Cannabis with alcohol was linked to worse driving, about the sum of each.
answers.but: Neither study measures crash risk or impairment on a road.

questions: Cannabis alone: are drivers who test positive more often in crashes?
answers.short: Drivers with cannabis in a test were linked to more crashes.
answers.but: These studies compare crashed drivers with others, so they cannot show one driver's chance of crashing.

questions: GHB or GBL with alcohol: what changes?
answers.short: People who took GHB with alcohol were less awake more often at hospital.
answers.but: Alcohol use was reported, not measured, and the amounts were not known.

questions: What does MDMA feel like?
answers.short: Mostly good: in lab studies, 67 in 100 called it positive afterwards. It lasted about four hours. Many also got a dry mouth or a clenched jaw.
answers.but: These were healthy volunteers in a lab, given a known pill and nothing else.

questions: Do nicotine patches and gum help people stop smoking?
answers.short: Nicotine patches, gum and similar help people who want to stop smoking.
answers.but: The gain is modest, and many trials were paid for by drug companies.

questions: What does smoking cannabis do to the lungs?
answers.short: Smoking cannabis is linked to cough, phlegm and wheeze; light smoking didn't lower lung function.
answers.but: Many people also smoked tobacco, so the studies can't say how much comes from cannabis.

questions: Are edibles a danger to young children?
answers.short: Calls to US poison centres about young children eating edibles rose about 15 times over, 2017 to 2021.
answers.but: These are only the calls that were made, and the study can't say why the number rose.

questions: What does a hangover do to my thinking the next day?
answers.short: The morning after heavy drinking, people remembered less and reacted slower than on alcohol-free days.
answers.but: The studies were small, and a short night's sleep may explain part of it.

questions: Do I drive worse the morning after, even with no alcohol left?
answers.short: Young drivers in a lab driving test drove worse after drinking nights than after alcohol-free nights.
answers.but: It was a driving machine in a lab, not real roads, and nobody checked how much they slept.

questions: Does drinking water while drinking alcohol stop a hangover?
answers.short: In one small test, men felt no better next morning when they had water between drinks than when they drank the same sake without it.
answers.but: Only 13 men took part, so a small benefit cannot be ruled out.

questions: Does mixing caffeine with alcohol change my hangover?
answers.short: People who drank beer with added caffeine had about the same hangover as those without caffeine.
answers.but: The study was small and did not test energy drinks.

questions: Does drinking beer before wine, or wine before beer, change my hangover?
answers.short: Drinking beer before wine or wine before beer gave about the same hangover.
answers.but: Only one kind of beer and one white wine were tested.

questions: Do people who take hangover pills drink more?
answers.short: Young adults who had used hangover pills reported more drinking problems than those who never had.
answers.but: A one-time survey cannot show whether the pills cause heavier drinking.

questions: Does paracetamol at usual doses harm the liver in people who drink?
answers.short: In short trials, paracetamol at usual doses did not raise a liver test more than dummy pills; some trials saw small, short-lived rises later.
answers.but: Most people in the trials had just stopped heavy drinking, and no trial tested paracetamol for a hangover.

questions: Is there a medicine that makes amphetamine withdrawal easier?
answers.short: In the four trials reviewed, no medicine clearly eased withdrawal or craving more than a dummy pill.
answers.but: The review found only four small trials, so a small benefit could have been missed.

questions: Does meth taken during the day spoil that night's sleep?
answers.short: After one of the larger doses, people slept less and worse that night than after a dummy dose.
answers.but: This was one small hospital study with single doses, not binges.

questions: How do you feel the morning after one dose of meth?
answers.short: Next morning, the biggest dose left people less alert and friendly than a dummy dose.
answers.but: Memory tests showed no change, but the study was small and printed no test results.

questions: Does exercise help low mood and worry after stopping meth?
answers.short: In one trial, exercise went with slightly less sadness and worry than health classes.
answers.but: Both groups got much better, and people knew their group, so hope may explain part.

questions: Does exercise make the urge to use meth weaker?
answers.short: Studies report less craving with exercise than without, but the review that lists them does not say how much less.
answers.but: We know these studies only through one weak review that gives no numbers.

questions: How does sleep change in the weeks after stopping cocaine?
answers.short: Over three weeks off cocaine, measured sleep got worse while people felt they slept better.
answers.but: One small study of 20 people in a hospital unit; daytime light and withdrawal from other drugs were not controlled.

questions: Can the medicine modafinil help sleep after stopping cocaine?
answers.short: In one small trial, modafinil helped people fall asleep faster than a dummy pill did.
answers.but: Only 20 people in hospital, and side effects like headache were more common on modafinil.

questions: Do clonidine or lofexidine help with opioid withdrawal?
answers.short: Yes: compared with a dummy pill, fewer people had bad withdrawal and more finished treatment.
answers.but: Only three small, old trials, mostly in hospital, and none with people coming off fentanyl.

questions: Is clonidine as good as slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?
answers.short: No clear difference in how many people finished, but clonidine-type medicines caused more low blood pressure and other side effects.
answers.but: The trials were small and some were badly run, so the answer could change.

questions: Does buprenorphine help people get through opioid withdrawal better than clonidine?
answers.short: Yes: more people finished withdrawal treatment with buprenorphine than with clonidine or lofexidine.
answers.but: No trial reported people coming off fentanyl, and two stopped early, which may have skewed the results.

questions: Is buprenorphine better than slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?
answers.short: They worked about the same: similar numbers of people finished withdrawal treatment with each.
answers.but: Only six small trials, mostly in hospitals or a prison.

questions: Is withdrawal from fentanyl worse than from heroin or other opioids?
answers.short: In one study, people coming off fentanyl had worse withdrawal than people coming off other opioids, such as heroin.
answers.but: The two groups were studied ten years apart, so something other than fentanyl may explain it.

questions: Does the ADHD medicine methylphenidate cause sleep problems?
answers.short: Children on methylphenidate had sleep problems recorded more often than children on a dummy pill.
answers.but: The review says how many times more often, not how many children out of 100.

questions: Does MDMA spoil sleep that night?
answers.short: After MDMA, people slept about two hours less than with a dummy pill, and had very little dreaming (REM) sleep.
answers.but: Only 7 people, one dose, in a quiet sleep lab, not a night out.

questions: Are you sleepier the day after MDMA?
answers.short: We don't know: next-day sleepiness after MDMA was not clearly different from a dummy pill.
answers.but: Only 7 people were tested, too few to rule out a difference.

questions: After high doses of DXM, how long is balance affected?
answers.short: After the highest doses, balance and coordination were still affected at the day's last test, while other effects were wearing off.
answers.but: Testing stopped there, so nobody knows when it ended, and nobody was tested next day.

questions: A month after high doses of DXM, any lasting effects?
answers.short: A month later, no one reported lasting upset or lasting changes in what they saw or heard.
answers.but: Only 12 carefully chosen volunteers, in a calm lab; people with psychosis or bipolar illness, themselves or in close family, could not take part.

questions: Will I sleep badly when I stop heroin or other opioids?
answers.short: Studies in one review found shorter, lighter sleep in the first weeks after stopping heroin than in good sleepers.
answers.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.

questions: Does alcohol help sleep, and what happens when I stop?
answers.short: Alcohol can help people fall asleep at first, but studies in one review found long heavy drinking leaves sleep poor for months.
answers.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.

questions: Will I sleep badly when I stop cannabis?
answers.short: Studies in one review found that many people who used cannabis regularly sleep badly after stopping, often with strange dreams.
answers.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.

questions: Can sleep medicines help when I stop alcohol, cannabis, cocaine or opioids?
answers.short: Some helped sleep, but better sleep did not reliably help people stay off drugs.
answers.but: This comes second-hand from a review that did not check how good the studies were.

questions: How does GHB affect driving?
answers.short: Soon after GHB, people crashed far more in a driving test than after a dummy drink.
answers.but: Only 16 people who had rarely or never used GHB, one dose, no alcohol, in a lab driving machine.

questions: Does GHB affect my memory or thinking afterwards?
answers.short: GHB affects memory while it works; in one study, people who had passed out from GHB many times had worse memory than other people who used GHB or other drugs.
answers.but: That one Dutch study cannot show GHB caused the memory problems, and nobody checked if they improve.

questions: How do people feel in the days and weeks after a psychedelic?
answers.short: Often better than before: less low mood and stress, more wellbeing, in most studies that checked. Some people got headaches, usually for a day or two, or slept badly.
answers.but: Most studies had no blind dummy-pill group, so nobody knows the cause, and most were supported sessions, not recreational use.

questions: Can I get flashbacks after LSD or psilocybin?
answers.short: About 1 in 11 lab volunteers reported a short flashback, mostly in the days after.
answers.but: These were healthy, screened volunteers in labs, with no drug-free group to compare.

questions: Is it dangerous to take loperamide (Imodium) to get through opioid withdrawal?
answers.short: It can be: some people who took very large amounts got serious heart-rhythm problems.
answers.but: These were only people seen by poisons doctors, who tend to see the sicker cases, and there was no group to compare with, so the study cannot show how often this happens.

questions: Do medicines for constipation caused by opioids work?
answers.short: Yes: compared with a dummy pill, more people's constipation got better.
answers.but: Nearly all the trials were in people taking opioids for pain; only one also included people dependent on opioids, so they say little about people using heroin or on methadone or buprenorphine treatment.

questions: Why do some people on methadone feel withdrawal before their next dose?
answers.short: In one small study, their methadone level tended to drop faster after its daily high point.
answers.but: Only 18 people were tested for one day, and by our check the difference fell just short of statistical significance, even after the authors left two people out.

questions: Can poppers damage your eyes?
answers.short: It seems so, in some people: reports describe blurry central vision and damage at the back of the eye.
answers.but: These are uncontrolled reports of people who saw an eye doctor, so they cannot prove poppers were the cause, or show how often it happens or which poppers do it.

questions: Can a benzodiazepine sleeping pill affect my driving the next day?
answers.short: Some benzodiazepine sleeping pills made people drive worse the next day than after dummy pills.
answers.but: Most studies tested one night in healthy volunteers, not people who take these pills for months.

questions: Taken nightly, do benzodiazepine sleeping pills still impair driving the next morning?
answers.short: For most pills the morning effect seemed smaller after several nights than after the first, but for some it lasted or grew over a week.
answers.but: The studies were small and short, and none followed people for more than about two weeks.

questions: Am I more likely to crash or fall when I start sleeping pills?
answers.short: Some studies found more crashes and falls soon after people started sleeping pills than without them; others did not.
answers.but: These studies watched what happened and cannot prove the pills caused the accidents.

questions: Does caffeine in the morning undo the effects of a sleeping pill?
answers.short: After a sleeping pill, morning caffeine left young men less sleepy than a dummy capsule did.
answers.but: Their test scores were not clearly better, and this study did not test driving.

questions: Do people feel more anxious or low when hungover?
answers.short: People felt more anxious and low when hungover than when sober, and also described guilt.
answers.but: The review does not say how big the changes were, and poor sleep or regret may explain part of them.

questions: Does anything help with the worry or low mood of a hangover?
answers.short: No study in the review tested a way to ease hangover worry; people said sharing the hangover with friends helped.
answers.but: These are people's own stories, not tests, so we cannot say what really helps.

questions: What does drinking before bed do to my dream sleep?
answers.short: After drinking, dream sleep started later and was shorter than on nights without alcohol.
answers.but: These were small sleep-lab studies, and the results were not the same in every study.

questions: Does a drink help me fall asleep or sleep longer?
answers.short: On average, alcohol before bed did not help people fall asleep faster than on nights without alcohol.
answers.but: Whether it changes how long people sleep is unclear, because the studies disagreed.

questions: Does caffeine during the day affect my sleep that night?
answers.short: After caffeine, people slept about 45 minutes less than on nights without caffeine.
answers.but: The people studied were healthy adults with low to moderate usual caffeine intake, so heavy users, teenagers and older adults may differ.

questions: If I suddenly go without my usual caffeine, will I get a headache?
answers.short: Without their usual caffeine, half got a headache by evening; people given caffeine pills did not.
answers.but: Only 40 hospital patients took part, and surgery itself can also cause headaches.

questions: Can caffeine pills in hospital stop the headache after an operation?
answers.short: In one small trial, fewer patients given caffeine pills had headaches after surgery than patients given dummy pills.
answers.but: The trial was small, so it cannot show whether the pills are safe for everyone.

questions: What does stopping smoking feel like, and for how long?
answers.short: After stopping smoking, people can feel grumpy, anxious and restless, and wake more at night, for weeks.
answers.but: This comes from one expert's summary of older studies; it does not say how many people get each feeling.

questions: What is the cocaine crash, and how long does it last?
answers.short: After a binge, people described a crash: very low mood, then long, heavy sleep and hunger.
answers.but: This is what some people in treatment told their doctors; it cannot show how often it happens.

questions: How do mood, craving and sleep change after stopping cocaine?
answers.short: In a closed research unit, men's low mood and craving were worst on the first day and eased over the next weeks.
answers.but: Only 12 men were studied, in a place with no cocaine and nothing to remind them of it.

questions: Do ADHD medicines like methylphenidate make it harder for children to sleep?
answers.short: On stimulant medicine, children took longer to fall asleep and slept less than on nights without it, sleep monitors showed.
answers.but: The review did not say by how many minutes, and mostly compared with nights before treatment began.

questions: Does melatonin help children on ADHD medicine fall asleep?
answers.short: Children on ADHD medicine fell asleep about 16 minutes sooner with melatonin than with a dummy pill.
answers.but: This was one small study of 19 children, paid for by the company that made the melatonin.

questions: How do you feel the day after taking ecstasy?
answers.short: People felt very tired and had slept less, but were not sadder than others.
answers.but: Two small studies; nobody tested the pills or measured sleep with a machine.

questions: Do people feel low a few days after taking ecstasy?
answers.short: Two small studies disagree, so they cannot say how often a mid-week low happens.
answers.but: Both studies were small, and only one measured people before they took ecstasy.

questions: Is your thinking different the day after LSD?
answers.short: A few small changes, some better and some worse, which may just be chance.
answers.but: One study of 24 people after one small lab dose; this report gives no mood or sleep data.

questions: Can a bad reaction to PCP last for weeks?
answers.short: In three reported cases, a severe breakdown lasted two to four weeks, then passed.
answers.but: Only three cases from 1975, and nobody tested the drugs they had taken.

questions: Does hospital medicine shorten a long breakdown after PCP?
answers.short: Nobody knows: in three cases, the medicines did not seem to shorten it.
answers.but: Three cases, with no comparison between treatments or with no treatment.

questions: How long does cannabis affect your driving skills?
answers.short: For several hours; probably longer after eating it than smoking it, and longer after bigger doses.
answers.but: These are averages from lab studies, not a safe time to drive for you.

questions: Do cannabis or CBD products taken by mouth help people sleep?
answers.short: In sleep labs, cannabis taken by mouth did not reliably change sleep, compared with a dummy pill or with sleep before treatment.
answers.but: Most were CBD or mild THC medicines for people with sleep problems; smoking was not tested.

questions: What happens to your sleep when you stop using a lot of cannabis?
answers.short: Sleep got shorter and slower to start, with more dream sleep, in the first nights.
answers.but: Three small studies, two of them from the 1970s with very strong lab doses.

questions: Does hot-pepper (capsaicin) cream ease cannabis-linked vomiting in hospital?
answers.short: Nobody knows yet: in small studies it sometimes helped and sometimes did not.
answers.but: One small fair test and four weaker studies, mostly at moderate to high risk of bias.

questions: Do medicines that block dopamine ease cannabis-linked vomiting in hospital?
answers.short: In two small studies, haloperidol eased sickness more than a usual anti-sickness medicine, and people given haloperidol or droperidol went home sooner than people given other care.
answers.but: Only two small studies, and both medicines can cause sudden muscle spasms.

questions: Is the day after worse with synthetic cannabis than with ordinary cannabis?
answers.short: People who had used both said synthetic cannabis gave a slightly worse hangover.
answers.but: These are memories from a 2011 online survey; nobody tested the products.

questions: Do fentanyl test strips show fentanyl when it is there?
answers.short: Almost always, in lab tests: 98 in 100 seized drug samples with fentanyl showed it on the strip.
answers.but: Lab staff did these tests, mostly with one brand. Testing at home was not studied.

questions: Can a fentanyl strip show fentanyl when there is none?
answers.short: Sometimes. Large amounts of meth, MDMA or two medicines made strips positive with no fentanyl there.
answers.but: These were lab tests, mostly of one drug at a time. How often it happens when people test their own drugs is not known.

questions: Do fentanyl strips pick up drugs related to fentanyl, like carfentanil?
answers.short: In lab tests, strips found most related drugs, but not all. Carfentanil needed large amounts.
answers.but: These were mostly pure drugs in water, tested by lab staff. The largest study reported no repeat tests.

questions: Do all fentanyl strips work the same?
answers.short: No. In lab tests, brands and batches differed. Some batches needed ten times more fentanyl.
answers.but: Each difference comes from one or two lab studies, and why batches differed is not known.

questions: Do nitazene test strips work?
answers.short: Mostly, in the lab. They picked up 24 of 33 kinds of nitazene but missed most desnitazenes, so a negative doesn't rule nitazenes out.
answers.but: Only pure or nearly pure drugs were tested, not mixed street drugs.

questions: Do xylazine test strips work?
answers.short: Yes, if there's at least as much xylazine as they're made to find: 37 of 38 such samples read positive. With less, only 6 of 28 did.
answers.but: It's one batch of strips, read in a lab, on residues from used equipment, not powders or pills.

questions: Do benzo test strips catch etizolam and other newer benzos?
answers.short: Not reliably. At drug-checking sites in Canada, strips caught newer benzos in 15 of 24 samples that had them, and just 8 of 16 with etizolam alone.
answers.but: A lab checked only some samples, not chosen at random: some were picked because of a suspected benzo overdose.

questions: Do colour tests like Marquis show whether a pill has MDMA in it?
answers.short: In a lab, experts got MDMA right. Two first-time testers made many mistakes.
answers.but: One small lab study from 2003, with a kit and pills of that time.

questions: Do take-home fentanyl strips match what trained staff find?
answers.short: For opioids, about the same. For meth and cocaine, take-home strips showed fentanyl far more often: 28 in 100 meth samples, against 5 in 100 tested by staff.
answers.but: The two groups tested different samples, and no lab checked which results were right.

questions: What can drug-checking strips and colour kits not tell you?
answers.short: A test for one drug did not show other drugs in the mix, or how much.
answers.but: Only two small studies tested this directly. The rest is how the tests are made.

questions: If people are given test strips, do they use them?
answers.short: It varies a lot. In different places, from 1 in 100 to 77 in 100.
answers.but: This is what people said or what services wrote down. Nobody checked.

questions: What do people do when a strip shows fentanyl?
answers.short: Some say they use less or go slower; many keep the same amount.
answers.but: This is what people said or planned. Nobody watched what they actually did.

questions: Do people throw drugs away when a test shows something unexpected?
answers.short: Sometimes. At one festival, 67 in 100 people handed over drugs that were not as sold.
answers.but: That was one festival, where chemists tested the drugs. After a strip showed fentanyl, few did.

questions: Do people who use test strips have fewer overdoses?
answers.short: No one knows yet. One study found no clear difference over four weeks.
answers.but: The result was too uncertain to rule out fewer or more overdoses.

questions: Do people keep using test strips over time?
answers.short: In the one study that lasted a year, fewer people had used a strip in the past month by the end than at the start.
answers.but: Many people left the study, and it did not find out why use fell.

questions: Did drug checking at a festival mean fewer hospital visits?
answers.short: We can't tell. Fewer people were taken to hospital for drugs, but other things changed too.
answers.but: One festival, one year before and one after, with no festival to compare.

questions: Are people who use test strips different from people who don't?
answers.short: Yes. In the largest US study, they more often injected and used fentanyl.
answers.but: This is what people said, and most were already using drug services.

questions: Can test kits do harm by making people feel falsely safe?
answers.short: No study has measured this. Riskier use after a positive strip was rare when asked.
answers.but: The studies said little about what people did after a strip showed no fentanyl.

questions: Did US states that legalised test strips see fewer drug deaths?
answers.short: After the law, drug deaths ran about 3 a year per 100,000 people below other states' trend.
answers.but: It looked at laws, not at people using strips. Other changes at the same time could explain it.

questions: Do people who drink a little live longer than people who don't drink?
answers.short: Many studies found slightly fewer deaths. Compared with people who never drank, there was no clear difference.
answers.but: Few studies made that comparison. So a small gain or a small loss is still possible.

questions: Is there an amount of alcohol with no health risk?
answers.short: Under 40, overall risk was lowest with almost no alcohol. Over 40, one model said half to two thirds of a drink a day.
answers.but: These are averages for whole populations, not one person's risk, and the over-40 dip rests on heart findings that gene studies mostly did not find.

questions: At what amount does drinking start to shorten life?
answers.short: Deaths rose above about 100 grams of alcohol a week. The comparison was with very light drinking.
answers.but: People who drank more also smoked more. The studies could only partly allow for that.

questions: Do people who drink a little have less heart disease?
answers.short: In many studies, people who drank a little had less heart disease than people who didn't.
answers.but: The group who didn't drink included people who had stopped, perhaps because they were ill, so alcohol may not be the reason.

questions: Do gene studies back the idea that alcohol protects the heart?
answers.short: The gene studies we read did not find that drinking a little protects the heart.
answers.but: Gene studies have possible biases of their own, and they cannot show what small amounts do.

questions: Do heavy drinking days change the heart risk?
answers.short: Heavy drinking days went with more heart disease than drinking the same amount evenly.
answers.but: This comes from one team's review of seven studies, and it does not say what counted as heavy.

questions: Does drinking raise the risk of stroke?
answers.short: In gene studies, more drinking went with more strokes, especially bleeding in the brain.
answers.but: For small amounts it is less clear: older studies found slightly fewer strokes, but the Chinese gene study did not.

questions: Does drinking raise blood pressure?
answers.short: People whose genes made them drink more had higher blood pressure.
answers.but: The studies do not say how many more people out of 100 get high blood pressure.

questions: Does drinking raise the risk of other heart and blood-vessel problems?
answers.short: In gene studies, more drinking went with more narrowed leg arteries; other results were unclear.
answers.but: These results come from two studies using the same UK volunteers, with few cases of some problems.

questions: Does drinking alcohol raise the risk of cancer?
answers.short: More drinking went with more mouth, throat, gullet, bowel, liver and breast cancer than not drinking.
answers.but: These studies watched groups of people, and about half did not take smoking or other differences into account.

questions: Does drinking a little raise the risk of cancer?
answers.short: Compared with not drinking, up to one drink a day went with slightly more of some cancers, fewer of others.
answers.but: The differences are so small that errors in reporting drinking, or other differences between the groups, could explain them.

questions: How many cancers are caused by alcohol?
answers.short: A model estimated that drinking caused about 4 in 100 new cancers worldwide in 2020.
answers.but: It is a computer estimate, not a count. It applies risks from studies of groups of people to every country.

questions: How much drinking raises the risk of liver cirrhosis?
answers.short: The more people drank, the higher their cirrhosis risk, compared with people who did not drink.
answers.but: How much the risk rose differed a lot between studies, and drinking was asked about only once.

questions: Is the cirrhosis risk from drinking different for women and men?
answers.short: At the same amount, studies found a bigger rise in cirrhosis risk for women than for men.
answers.but: No study tested the difference, and much of the evidence on women comes from one old American study.

questions: For the same amount, is drinking every day worse for the liver?
answers.short: In one study, men who drank daily had more cirrhosis than men drinking 2 to 4 days a week.
answers.but: People who drank daily also drank more, and the study could not fully separate how often from how much.

questions: How many deaths does alcohol cause worldwide?
answers.short: Global models estimated alcohol caused about 2.3 to 2.8 million deaths a year, compared with no one drinking.
answers.but: These are computer estimates built on studies of groups of people, not counted deaths.

questions: How common is alcohol use disorder?
answers.short: In a US survey, 14 in 100 adults had it in the past year.
answers.but: Another US survey found a little over half as many, so the number depends on the survey.

questions: How many people with alcohol use disorder get help?
answers.short: In a US survey, 20 in 100 people who ever had it sought help.
answers.but: People said this themselves, and the survey left out most people who were in treatment.

questions: What are the DTs (delirium tremens), and how often do they happen?
answers.short: Sudden confusion in alcohol withdrawal; a few in 100 people in hospital get it.
answers.but: Most figures are passed on by one review or come from old trials, mostly one from 1969.

questions: Do medicines prevent seizures in alcohol withdrawal?
answers.short: In old trials, benzodiazepines cut seizures: about 1 in 100, against 8 on dummy pills.
answers.but: The trials were from the 1960s to 1983, and few people had seizures.

questions: Does naltrexone help people drink less?
answers.short: On naltrexone, 46 in 100 went back to heavy drinking, against 54 on dummy pills.
answers.but: Most people in the trials were middle-aged men who had already stopped drinking and had counselling.

questions: Does acamprosate help people stop drinking?
answers.short: In trials, 76 in 100 on acamprosate drank again, against 83 on dummy pills.
answers.but: The most carefully run trials found no clear difference.

questions: Do topiramate, disulfiram or other medicines help people drink less?
answers.short: Topiramate was linked to fewer drinking days; disulfiram showed no clear benefit in blinded trials.
answers.but: Most of these medicines were tested in only a few trials.

questions: Does talking therapy add anything to naltrexone for alcohol problems?
answers.short: In one large trial, adding talking therapy to naltrexone did not help more.
answers.but: It was one US trial, not built to test combinations.

questions: How many pregnant women drink alcohol?
answers.short: About 10 in 100 pregnant women worldwide drank some alcohol. By region, from under 1 to 25.
answers.but: Most countries had too few studies, so a model filled them in. Women may not report all drinking.

questions: How common are fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) and fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS)?
answers.short: About 8 in 1,000 children are thought to have FASD. About 1.5 in 1,000 people have FAS.
answers.but: Few countries had counted it. Most numbers were worked out from how many women said they drank.

questions: How did doctors first spot fetal alcohol syndrome?
answers.short: In 1973, doctors described 8 children of mothers who drank heavily. All grew poorly and developed slowly.
answers.but: Some children were picked because they had these signs. They were not compared with other children.

questions: How much of a ketamine dose reaches the blood, and how fast?
answers.short: Nearly all of an injected dose reaches the blood. Swallowed, only about a sixth does.
answers.but: Both figures come from four people each, in one study from 1982.

questions: How much ketamine reaches the blood by nose, tongue or suppository?
answers.short: In three men, the nose spray reached the blood best, then tongue and suppository.
answers.but: Only three men took part, and two of the methods were not carried out as described.

questions: How long does ketamine stay in the blood?
answers.short: It drops fast at first, then falls by half every two to three hours.
answers.but: The two studies had only six and three people, and timed mainly doses into a vein.

questions: What do brain scans show while someone is given ketamine?
answers.short: In scans, brain activity went up, not down, most of all at the front.
answers.but: The scans show one session only, and cannot show which brain change causes which feeling.

questions: Do the two mirror-image forms of ketamine, S and R, do different things?
answers.short: In one small study the S form caused psychosis-like effects; the R form did not.
answers.but: Only ten people took part, and everyone could tell when they had been given a drug.

questions: Does ketamine affect memory and thinking that night, and 3 days later?
answers.short: That night, memory scores were far below other partygoers'. Three days later the gap was mostly gone.
answers.but: Two small studies by one team, and nobody tested what people had taken.

questions: Does using ketamine often affect memory, even days later?
answers.short: On some memory tests, people who used ketamine most days did worse than others.
answers.but: They also had less schooling. Nobody was tested before they started.

questions: Does memory improve when people cut down or stop frequent ketamine use?
answers.short: Nobody knows yet. People who had stopped did as well as people who don't use it.
answers.but: The people who had stopped had mostly used less, and nobody was tested before starting.

questions: Is using ketamine often linked to low mood, feeling detached or unusual beliefs?
answers.short: People who used ketamine most days more often reported unusual beliefs, feeling detached or feeling low.
answers.but: Mostly mild. Nobody was asked before they started, so the cause is not known.

questions: What does ketamine do to memory and attention while it is working?
answers.short: People remembered far fewer words than on their salt-water day. An hour after it stopped, scores matched.
answers.but: Small studies, 14 to 18 people each, and no study checked that the raters stayed unaware.

questions: What happened when people with schizophrenia were given ketamine in a study?
answers.short: In nine patients, symptoms rose for twenty minutes, then returned to their usual level.
answers.but: Nine people, one study, and staff chose the order of the days instead of leaving it to chance.

questions: What does ketamine do to perception, thinking and the sense of self while it is working?
What does ketamine do to perception, thinking and sense of self?
answers.short: Compared with a salt-water day, people felt cut off from themselves and their thinking got muddled.
answers.but: Raters could probably tell who had ketamine, and the studies disagree a lot about how big the effects are.

questions: How does ketamine work in the brain?
answers.short: It blocks a docking point for the brain's main go-signal, called the NMDA receptor.
answers.but: Nearly all these numbers come from animals and from cells in dishes, and reach us through reviews.

questions: Do people who use cannabis often do worse on memory and thinking tests?
answers.short: On average they score a little lower than people who use little or none.
answers.but: People were tested only after they had started, so the studies can't show that cannabis caused it.

questions: Do memory and thinking differences last after people stop using cannabis?
answers.short: Not clear. Where studies asked people to stop for over 3 days, the gap was small.
answers.but: This compared different studies, not the same people before and after they stopped.

questions: Does using cannabis as a teenager lower IQ later in life?
answers.short: Not shown either way. In one study, people dependent for years lost about 6 IQ points.
answers.but: Other differences between people could explain it. Twin studies of lighter use found no clear extra loss.

questions: Is teenage cannabis use linked to depression or anxiety later?
answers.short: Teens who used cannabis the most were a bit more often depressed later than teens who didn't.
answers.but: These studies can't show that cannabis caused it; other differences between the teens may explain it.

questions: Is teenage cannabis use linked to suicidal thoughts or attempts?
answers.short: Teens who used cannabis the most reported suicidal thoughts or attempts more often than teens who didn't.
answers.but: Only three studies each, mostly measured in the teen years; they cannot show cause.

questions: Is using cannabis in pregnancy linked to a smaller baby, early birth or intensive care?
Is cannabis in pregnancy linked to smaller babies or intensive care?
answers.short: Babies were a bit lighter, and more of them went to intensive care after birth.
answers.but: Many mothers also smoked or drank. Most studies could not tell this apart from cannabis.

questions: Is cannabis linked to heart attacks and strokes?
answers.short: Some studies link it to heart attacks and strokes; a 25-year study found no link.
answers.but: These figures come from reviews. The studies could not fully tell cannabis and tobacco apart.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help long-lasting pain?
answers.short: Slightly: about half a point less pain out of 10 than with a dummy medicine.
answers.but: The trials were short, mostly tested one mouth spray, and many had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines ease muscle stiffness in multiple sclerosis (MS)?
answers.short: People felt a little less stiff than with a dummy, but doctors' tests showed no clear change.
answers.but: The trials were short, most often tested one mouth spray, and many had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help with sickness from chemotherapy?
answers.short: In three small trials, more people had their sickness fully controlled than with a dummy.
answers.but: Only 102 people were in these three trials, and most trials had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help sleep, anxiety, appetite or other conditions?
answers.short: Too few small trials to tell; sleep scores were slightly better than with a dummy.
answers.but: Each condition had only a few small trials. Many had serious weaknesses.

questions: What side effects do cannabis medicines cause?
answers.short: More side effects than with a dummy, such as dizziness, feeling high, confusion and dry mouth.
answers.but: Short trials at the highest dose tested; long-term harms were not studied.

questions: How many people who use cannabis become dependent on it?
answers.short: About 9 in 100 people who ever tried it, in two older US surveys.
answers.but: The surveys are from 1990 to 2005 and used a narrower definition than today's.

questions: Are frequent use and starting young linked to cannabis dependence?
answers.short: People who use more often are more often dependent; for starting young, studies disagree.
answers.but: Most numbers come second-hand from reviews, and none can show what causes what.

questions: How common is withdrawal when people who use cannabis regularly stop, and what is it like?
How common is cannabis withdrawal, and what is it like?
answers.short: About 17 in 100 in general surveys; more than half in clinic and hospital groups.
answers.but: Studies counted it in different ways, and none checked how often people get these feelings anyway.

questions: What is cannabis hyperemesis syndrome (repeated severe vomiting), and does stopping end it?
answers.short: Bouts of severe vomiting with regular cannabis use; in reported cases, stopping ended them.
answers.but: Published cases only: nobody knows how common it is, and fewer than half were followed up.

questions: How does THC move through the body after smoking and after eating, and how long does it stay in blood and urine?
How fast does THC rise and fall in the blood, smoked or eaten?
answers.short: Smoked, THC peaks in the blood within minutes; eaten, it rises slowly over hours.
answers.but: Old, small lab studies of weak cannabis, described in one review.

questions: Can cannabis cause psychosis, and does using it daily matter?
answers.short: People who use cannabis, most of all daily, get psychosis more often than people who don't.
answers.but: This is a link: these studies cannot show that cannabis was the cause.

questions: Is strong cannabis more closely linked to psychosis than weaker cannabis?
answers.short: Daily use of strong types had the strongest link with psychosis, but the gap from weaker types could be chance.
answers.but: Strength was guessed from the type people named, and both studies come from one team.

questions: Does cannabis cause psychosis, or could something else explain the link?
answers.short: Not known. Part of the link seems to come from other differences between people.
answers.but: The gene studies only looked at ever trying cannabis, not at daily or strong use.

questions: Has schizophrenia become more common as more people used cannabis?
answers.short: Studies disagree: some places saw more psychosis over time, others no rise as use grew.
answers.but: We know these studies only through reviews, and changes in diagnosis can blur trends.

questions: Does how I feel beforehand change how a psychedelic trip goes?
answers.short: It may. Feeling calm, open and ready beforehand went with easier trips, and feeling anxious went with more anxiety during the trip.
answers.but: These are links: no study we read changed how people felt beforehand to test it.

questions: Do the place and the people around me affect a psychedelic trip?
answers.short: Maybe a little. In surveys, people who felt safe and supported reported slightly fewer hard moments.
answers.but: People rated this looking back, and the one study that asked beforehand found only a weak link.

questions: Does the kind of ayahuasca ceremony matter for how it goes?
answers.short: Maybe a little. People who felt safer and better supported at their last ceremony recalled a bit less fear. They also reported fewer problems later.
answers.but: One survey: people rated the ceremony and how it went at the same time, looking back.

questions: How common are bad trips, and can problems last?
answers.short: Fairly common: 41 in 100 people who'd used psychedelics recalled at least one difficult trip. 5 in 100 said one had badly affected their daily life.
answers.but: That's one online survey, and people were looking back over their whole lives.

questions: Does music change how a trip goes?
answers.short: Nobody knows for sure: no study we read compared music with silence. 18 of 19 patients said music helped at times; 10 said it sometimes made things harder.
answers.but: The one test that compared two playlists had just 10 people, so it could easily miss a difference.

questions: Does music change how a ketamine treatment session goes?
answers.short: Nobody knows yet whether it changes how a session feels or how well ketamine works. One trial found the top blood pressure number rose about 7 points less with music.
answers.but: Just 32 patients; the report gave no results on how the sessions felt.

questions: Do some people feel MDMA more strongly than others?
answers.short: Yes. The biggest link was the amount per kilo of body weight. Given the same amount, lighter people got more per kilo, which went with stronger effects.
answers.but: That's one lab, with healthy volunteers in a hospital, most of them trying MDMA for the first time.

questions: Do some people feel LSD more strongly than others?
answers.short: In lab studies, the dose went most with how strong LSD felt. Mood and personality did too.
answers.but: The paper says which way each link goes, not how big it is.

questions: Which harm reduction services exist for benzos, and do they work?
answers.short: Drug checking, prescribed benzos and stricter rules exist. No study has shown whether they lower harm.
answers.but: The review did not judge how good the studies were, and most had no comparison group.

questions: How common is using drugs alone, and why do people do it?
answers.short: Very common: 76 in 100 people at harm reduction sites said they'd used alone at least once in the past week. The most-picked reason: it's easier and more comfortable at home.
answers.but: It's one survey in one part of Canada, of people who already went to these sites.

questions: Does CBD taken with THC change THC's effects?
answers.short: Studies disagree on CBD and THC; no reliable pattern has been shown across different conditions.
answers.but: The studies used different amounts and timings. Most were small, and earlier trials were read through a review.

questions: Do drug and alcohol problems develop faster in women than in men?
answers.short: Not shown for women in general. It was seen mostly in people in treatment.
answers.but: All these studies rest on memory. People said years later how old they were at each step.

questions: Are women less likely than men to get alcohol or drug treatment?
answers.short: For alcohol, somewhat less likely, mostly years after problems start. For drugs, about the same.
answers.but: The surveys are from the US, and people remembered dates years later.

questions: In drug or alcohol treatment, do women do as well as men?
answers.short: Most large studies found no difference between women and men once in treatment.
answers.but: This comes from two reviews by one research group; we have not read the studies themselves.

questions: Do genes and the home you grow up in shape drug problems?
answers.short: Both are linked: what comes from birth parents, and the home a child grows up in.
answers.but: One Swedish study. What birth parents pass on includes the pregnancy, not just genes.

questions: Do words about drug use change how others see a person?
answers.short: Yes, some do. People judged a person more harshly when their troubles were said to come from drug use, not a health concern.
answers.but: These are views given after one made-up story, not how people who use drugs are really treated.

questions: Does drinking at a young age lead to alcohol problems later on?
answers.short: Not known. Some of the link seems to come from things that lead to both.
answers.but: Only a few small studies followed young people over time; the big survey relied on memory.

questions: How often do people who use cocaine also drink or use cannabis?
answers.short: On average, about 3 in 4 also used alcohol, and 4 to 6 in 10 cannabis.
answers.but: These averages mix very different studies, from about 1 in 10 to nearly all.

questions: Can caffeine bring on panic attacks in people with panic disorder?
answers.short: About half had a panic attack after one big dose; none after a dummy.
answers.but: Most studies used one large amount. The review cannot show what ordinary smaller servings do.

questions: Does eating before drinking change blood alcohol?
answers.short: In 9 men, a meal just before drinking roughly halved peak blood alcohol.
answers.but: One small lab study of young men. It measured blood alcohol, without testing impairment.

questions: Can sniffing solvents cause sudden death?
answers.short: Sudden deaths after sniffing solvents and sprays were reported in one old survey.
answers.but: It counted deaths, without measuring risk among everyone who used these products.

questions: Do official counts miss drug deaths?
answers.short: Some deaths are missing; others are counted without showing which drug was involved.
answers.but: The gaps differ by place and rules. Most evidence concerns older US opioid deaths.

questions: Do official counts miss heroin deaths?
answers.short: In the places studied, closer reviews linked more deaths to heroin than records did.
answers.but: Each review used its own rules for what counts as a heroin death.

questions: Do autopsies and drug tests change which deaths count as drug deaths?
answers.short: Sometimes: at one centre, about 10 in 100 suspected drug deaths had another cause.
answers.but: Only two US places have been studied, so other places may differ.

questions: Does how the news describes a drug death change what readers think?
answers.short: Yes, somewhat. Readers judged the person who died more harshly when the story said heroin, not ecstasy, or an older person with years of use.
answers.but: Readers saw one made-up story and answered straight away; nobody checked what they did later.

questions: Did news stories about mephedrone deaths get the facts right?
answers.short: Not always: several deaths blamed on it in the news had other causes.
answers.but: One study, and the later test results are second-hand reports, not official records.

questions: Can drug levels change after death?
answers.short: Yes. Levels can rise or fall after death and differ between blood vessels, so a drug can look more or less involved in a death than it was.
